'''''Dendrobium hekouense''''' is a miniature species of [[orchid]].<ref name="curtis-botanicals">{{cite journal |last1=Cribb, Averyanov, Schuiteman, Want |title=973. Dendrobium Hekouense |journal=Curtis's Botanical Magazine |date=March 2021 |volume=38 |pages=82–88 |doi=10.1111/curt.12375 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/curt.12375 |access-date=11 February 2024|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
The primary habitat of ''Dendrobium hekouense'' is evergreen forests located in subtropical highlands.  These forests are covered with dense fog between April and October as a result of monsoon weather.<ref name="annales-botanici">{{cite journal |last1=Liu, Chen |title=Dendrobium hekouense (Orchidaceae), a new species from Yunnan, China |journal=Annales Botanici Fennici |date=March 2011 |volume=48 |pages=87–90 |doi=10.5735/085.048.0114 |s2cid=86823517 |url=https://www.sekj.org/PDF/anb48-free/anb48-087i.pdf |access-date=11 February 2024}}</ref>

It was first described in [[Yunnan]], [[China]] and has also been found in Northern [[Vietnam]].<ref name="curtis-botanicals" />  

==Characteristics==
''Dendrobium hekouense'' forms a single-flower [[inflorescence]] that arises from a leafless [[pseudobulb]].<ref name="annales-botanici"/>  

In its natural habitat this orchid flowers between August and September, during a period that coincides with annual rain.  It is typically found on the ground-facing side of tree trunks, in a position that prevents rainwater from falling into the flower.<ref name="annales-botanici"/>
